notes.text: The sheet is headed Exercice 4.10.6. It specifies a U-site S with topology less fine than the canonical topology and a collection of arrows with properties a)–d). No date or own manuscript page number is visible. The pencilled 9 in the lower left corner is treated as the archive sheet number.
notes.basis: Observation of heading, opening, conditions a–d, and lower-left margin; descriptive transcription only.

notes.text: The definition of the petit site S(X) is revised by cancelling “considérons le site” and adding “notons”, cancelling “dont la catégorie sous-jacente est” and adding “constitué par”, and inserting “le site” from the left margin with matching looped signs. The described subcategory consists of objects of S/X whose structural morphism lies in the underlined collection, with topology induced from S.
notes.basis: Observation of definition paragraph and crop 05–06; no claim about the identity of the correcting hand.

notes.text: Item 1 asks that the covering families with arrows in the collection form a pretopology generating the topology of S. Item 2 asks for continuity of base change and names its corresponding functor on sheaf categories. The reference after the display ends with “iv)).”; both closing parentheses are present.
notes.basis: Observation of items 1–2 and their display. No proof checking was performed.

notes.text: Item 3 asks for an equivalence between the topos marked S with a superscript tilde and a category of systems (F_X), (phi_u), then starts specifying their transition morphisms. This page ends at “ces systèmes” with no ending punctuation; no continuation was consulted.
notes.basis: Observation of item 3, its display, and final two source lines.

notes.text: The epsilon-shaped index sign is retained by contour, despite its membership role. The foreground handwritten M is distinguished from its uncertain S-shaped underprint; two typed S/M superpositions remain uncertain in order. The doubled O in “On” is represented under the supplied double-strike convention, without inventing an earlier different letter. These are ink-reading decisions, not mathematical repairs.
notes.basis: Crops 02–04, 07–08. No mathematical check events occurred in this reader run.
